Left OPEN for the desk/walker with this exercise; no fix invented.

A member's private mood check-in moved the shared affect state that chat, council and agent policy derive from. Mechanism, exercised end to end at branch state: the ATS middleware keys sessions per authenticated user (user_<id>, its own comment: prevents 'shared mood' across users) and server-internal reads use that session — but POST /api/affect/event and /api/affect/reset resolved the session from the request BODY first, and the affect lens's AffectSessionProvider defaulted its sessionId to the literal 'default', so MoodTracker's S-AFF-1 emit (and every panel read) landed in the one shared 'default' session; one check-in's FEEDBACK event (intensity 0.50, polarity +0.50) moved its Valence 50 to 56.2 with Arousal, Coherence and Trust — the ticket's exact numbers. Fix (cf8b787c5): both write routes now resolve req._atsSessionId FIRST (a body field can no longer steer a write into a shared or another user's session); the session context defaults to '' (no named session — reads fall back to the caller's own server-keyed session); the session strip's clear-field path returns to '' instead of 'default'. S-AFF-1's intent is preserved: your own state still moves with your own acts — it is no longer everyone's state. A deliberately named session can still be VIEWED (GET routes keep their param), but writes always land in the caller's own session. Pins: server/tests/affect-session-isolation.test.js 5/5 on the fixed tree, 1 pass / 4 fail on the pristine control (the pass is the unchanged middleware keying); affect-policy-derivations green; FE affect panels 3/4 in the borrowed env with the single failure (ChartKit render) proven identical on pristine files — pre-existing env noise. Reference shape matched: the platform-internal gate's server-mirrored identity rule (CB-0402) — the server, not the client, owns the caller's identity.

Invoice create and Mark paid posted no journal entries, no audit log, and no revenue or cash change — AR never reached the ledger. Premise exercised in code: invoice-create pushed only the invoice row and invoice-mark-paid only flipped its status, while the same domain file carries a complete double-entry journal (je-post with CoA validation, balance guard and recordAudit) the invoice actions never called. Fix: an internal postInvoiceJournal helper in je-post's exact entry shape (source 'accounting-invoice', sourceId = the invoice id, audit-logged via recordAudit) — invoice-create posts Dr Accounts Receivable (acct_1100) / Cr Sales Revenue (acct_4000) at the invoice total dated issuedAt and stamps invoice.journalEntryId; invoice-mark-paid posts Dr Cash (acct_1000) / Cr AR dated paidAt, refuses to double-post (a repeat mark-paid returns alreadyPaid with no entry), and books the recognition leg first for legacy invoices created before postings existed; invoice-void of an open invoice posts the reversal (Dr Revenue / Cr AR) so no phantom receivable or revenue survives. invoice-credit-note's journal leg is named, not built: it operates on already-paid invoices and its refund-payable account shape is a desk call. Tests: server/tests/accounting-invoice-journal.test.js 4/4 on the fixed tree and 0/4 on the pristine control; accounting-domain-parity stays green (95/95 together). Reference matched: the domain's own je-post entry + audit shape, no new machinery.

Exercised end to end at branch state: the builder lets a user author workflows whose default trigger is 'button_click' (WorkflowBuilder, workflowSave), but NOTHING executes a workflow anywhere — there is no workflow-run action in server/domains/appmaker.js (only workflowOptions / workflowSave / workflowDelete), and previewRender emits purely static HTML: its button element is a handler-less <button> with no script in the document at all, inside an iframe sandboxed 'allow-same-origin' without allow-scripts. Two adjacent facts from the same exercise: (1) data bindings are stored on the element expressly 'so previewRender can surface them' (dataBindElement) but renderEl never reads el.binding — a smaller unwired renderer leg the desk can scope separately; (2) the ticket's reload leg does not reproduce from code — editorSavePage persists elements faithfully (500 cap, props intact) and the canvas and preview both read the same saved pages, so the 'few shapes after reload' observation needs a live repro with the project id to chase further. Left OPEN with this exercise; no fix invented.

Transit stops lived only in TransitCoveragePanel's useState — parcels in the same workspace load from the persisted parcel store on mount, stops started empty every mount and were never saved, so a reload dropped every stop (the ticket's repro: analysis ran, stop absent after reload). Fix mirrors the lens's own parcel pattern (the matched in-product reference, and the ticket's stated expectation: 'Stop persists like parcels, scenarios and projects do'): server/domains/urbanplanning.js gains a per-user stops store in the same urbanPlanningLens state (stop-add with coordinate validation and a bounded mode set, stop-list, stop-remove — the parcel trio's exact shape, saveUpState on every mutation), and the panel loads stops on mount, adds through stop-add (speaking a save refusal inline instead of pretending), and removes through stop-remove. Evidence: new server/tests/urban-planning-stops-persist.test.js 4/4 (add→list round trip scoped per owner, invalid coordinates refused with nothing stored, mode fallback, remove + stranger not_found) against a 0/4 pristine control (actions unregistered before the fix); the existing urban-planning suites (full-build, lens-macros, mentalhealth parity) pass 81/81 with the fix. Budget 'Spent' aggregated only the manual expense log — project-list's per-project spent and the dashboard's totalSpent both summed project.expenses and nothing else, while shopping-toggle flipped a purchased flag no aggregation read, so the walker's purchased  x 2 = 8 left Spent at /bin/bash exactly as filed. Fix makes the server the single aggregation source (matched reference: the lens's own shopping-list, which already totals purchased items as line totals): project-list now adds each project's purchased items (price x qty) into its spent with the portion exposed as shoppingSpent, and reports purchased items with no (or a deleted) project as unassignedShoppingSpent instead of dropping them; the dashboard's totalSpent includes all purchased shopping with shoppingSpent broken out. BudgetPanel's headline Spent adds the unassigned bucket to the per-project sum, so an unassigned purchase counts without inventing a project for it. Un-purchasing removes the amount again; manual expenses are untouched and cannot double-count a purchase (the toggle never wrote an expense). Evidence: new server/tests/home-improvement-shopping-spent.test.js 4/4 (the walker's exact 8 case, project-assigned roll-in, toggle-off reversal, expenses alongside purchases at 54 = 30 + 24) against a 0/4 pristine control; home-improvement parity suite green 25/25 in the same run.

Premise convicted in-tree: the Art editor's canvas save posted the PNG as a base64 data field through the JSON /api/media/upload route, and the endpoint's own comment names the trap — the global sanitizer cuts every JSON string at 10,000 chars (~7,500 bytes), so any real drawing arrived truncated; the endpoint honestly refuses 413 upload_truncated and directs callers to POST /api/media/upload-raw, the transport the music and photography uploads already use — the art save was the one caller still on the doomed route, and its failure surfaced only as a generic toast. The save now mirrors the platform pattern (new lib/art/upload.ts on the photography shape): canvas.toBlob -> the blob IS the request body to /api/media/upload-raw with title/filename/mediaType/tags on the query, Content-Type image/png, no JSON cap; failures toast the specific server wording via describeArtUploadError (413 names the size, 401 names sign-in) instead of the bare 'Failed to save artwork'. Evidence: new tests/art-canvas-save-raw-003.test.tsx mounts the real desk in canvas mode with a 9,000-byte stub PNG (deliberately over the survival size), clicks Save, and asserts the post goes to upload-raw with the blob body and never to the JSON route; on the pristine desk the same test fails (the save never reaches the raw route). The server's own media-upload-raw suite already pins the receiving end, including the upload_truncated refusal this ticket filed.

Premise confirmed twice over: the walker's KJFK lookup died with 'airport lookup failed: fetch failed' on prod, and at fix time the same API call failed from this seat's independent egress (TLS completes, api.aviationapi.com drops the request; the parent site and other hosts answer normally). The structural defect is in-tree: airport-lookup depended on ONE free API for the primary record even though aviation.js's own header promised an OurAirports CC0 fallback 'for international airports' that was never built. The fallback is now built as documented: the CC0 airports.csv fetched once, indexed by ident/gps_code/iata_code, process-cached with a 10-minute failure cooldown, consulted on a primary throw, a primary HTTP error, and a primary not-found — and it only replaces the outcome when it actually finds the airport (name/city/lat/lng/elevation in the primary's result shape, runways/frequencies honestly empty, source labelled as the fallback). When both sources fail or miss, the primary's original error stands verbatim. Evidence: live check at fix time — the CC0 dataset answers and carries KJFK with its real fields; new server/tests/aviation-airport-fallback-005.test.js 4/4 (throw->fallback resolves KJFK; not-found->fallback resolves EGLL and by IATA LHR; both-down->original error verbatim; neither->not-found wording) vs 2/4 on the pristine domain; the aviation parity suite is unchanged (63/64 both pristine and fixed — the one failure, an Open-Meteo winds-aloft parse, pre-exists at the slice base). If aviationapi.com recovers, the primary path is byte-identical to before.

Premise convicted at the contract seam: QualityLoopPanel counted a DTU as scored whenever creti was truthy, but /api/dtus serializes creti as summary TEXT (dtuForClient emits cretiHuman prose) while cri's server contract (normDtu) keeps creti only as an OBJECT of numeric dimension scores — so the header read 'N/N DTUs scored' and the Compare dropdowns populated with DTUs the server could only refuse ('both DTUs must have CRETI scores'), with no empty state anywhere: the walker's blank pane. There is also no producer of cri-shaped scores anywhere in the platform (the name covers three different shapes — generateCRETI's text structure, concord-shield's 0-20 threat dims, and cri's 0-1 quality dims — and nothing computes cri's five dims for a DTU), so a real comparison awaits a scorer build, named here not invented. The fix applies the server's contract in the panel: scored now requires a creti object with at least one numeric CRETI dimension (the header and every scored-fed tab tell the truth), and Compare renders the ticket's accepted second leg — a clear empty state ('No scored DTUs to compare yet', with the one-scored variant worded so) — instead of populated-looking dropdowns whose only outcome was silence. With genuinely scored DTUs the compare flow is untouched. Evidence: new tests/cri-compare-002.test.tsx 2/2 — the real text-creti corpus shape counts 0 scored and shows the empty state, and an object-scored corpus compares end to end; on the pristine panel the first case fails (2/2 claimed, no empty state) and the second passes, so the pin discriminates the defect from the flow.

INVESTIGATED at B5 (slice) — premise TRUE and structural: detective cases are crimes recorded by the world simulation (crime-engine.recordCrime via world events; detective.list reads listOpenCrimes for the chosen world), and the lens is a pure consumer (list/get/evidence/deduce). No case generator or seeder exists anywhere — no macro or lib function fabricates a standalone solvable case (suspects + evidence + a culprit satisfying deduce's 2-of-3 + suspect_match rule) for a world whose simulation has produced no crime — so on concordia-hub, with zero open crimes on record, the board's (already honest, B3 F2) empty state is a dead end with no create/generate control, exactly as filed. The cure is a case-generation build: a generator that fabricates a solvable case into the crimes store for a chosen world, with the solvability guarantee the deduction rule implies — gameplay-design surface (difficulty, evidence spread, culprit consistency), priced for the desk/build queue rather than invented inside a fix slice. The row carries the substrate map (detective macros -> lib/detective.listOpenCrimes -> crimes table <- crime.record from world events) as the build's starting evidence.

The gate itself is founder-ruled design and is NOT touched: entity.terminal is hard-disabled unless the operator enables it (server.js P0.1 gate; the sandbox stays operator/sovereign-only). The defect is presentation, in the ticket's own terms ('Tab usable or hidden with explanation'): the Terminal tab presented as fully usable — live input, Run button, a 'Ready' line promising council votes — and the explanation arrived only AFTER a command was run, worded as a raw operator instruction naming the env var. The tab now probes the gate once on mount (an empty command is side-effect-free precisely because the macro's gate answers before any validation or execution), and when the gate is closed it renders the explanation up front in member wording ('Terminal execution is turned off on this server by the operator, so commands cannot run here'), replaces the Ready line, and disables the input and Run button; the post-run disabled line speaks the same sentence instead of the env instruction. When the gate is open the tab behaves exactly as before. Evidence: new tests/entity-terminal-gate-011.test.tsx mounts the real inspector with the macro returning the disabled shape — the banner renders without any command being run, the input is disabled, and no env-var text appears anywhere; it fails on the pristine inspector.
